title: Sequence-to-Sequence and Attention
overview: Encoder-decoder models map one sequence to another, such as translation. Attention lets the decoder look back at all encoder states instead of one fixed vector.
objectives: Describe why attention removes the fixed-vector bottleneck

method.title: Encoder-decoder
method.body: The encoder reads the input into states; the decoder generates output tokens one at a time.

method.title: Bottleneck
method.body: Compressing a whole sentence into one vector loses information for long inputs.

method.title: Attention
method.body: At each step the decoder scores every encoder state, softmaxes the scores and takes the weighted sum as context.

method.title: Alignment
method.body: Attention weights often reveal which input positions matter for each output token.

pseudocode:
scores = [dot(dec_h, enc_h[i]) for i in range(T)]
alpha = softmax(scores)
context = sum(alpha[i] * enc_h[i] for i in range(T))
next_token = decoder_step(dec_h, context)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
enc = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])  # 3 encoder states
dec = np.array([1.0, 0.0])                            # decoder query
scores = enc @ dec
alpha = np.exp(scores) / np.exp(scores).sum()
context = alpha @ enc
print("scores:", scores)
print("attention weights:", np.round(alpha, 3))
print("context:", np.round(context, 3))
